IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r3.speaker: آخر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r3.claim: An unnamed interpreter says al-masājid are the bodily limbs on which a person prostrates, listing the forehead, hands, knees, and feet.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r3.anchor: وقال آخر في قوله: {وأن المساجد لله} (3) إنها الآراب التي يسجد عليها المرء؛ وهي جبهته ويداه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r3.claim: The direct warning to Quraysh recalls tawḥīd: since God alone can be worshipped, alleged deities cannot rescue them, and they must not pollute the mosque by worshipping them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r3.anchor: the Quraysh are directly addressed and warned of the sanctity a mosque has in which no one but God is worshipped

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r4.claim: Mosques are reserved for God by their very purpose: neither may one be built for another nor may anyone else be worshipped there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r4.anchor: Neither can a mosque be built for someone other than God nor can someone other than Him be worshipped in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r5.claim: Though unspecified, “mosques” likely refers to the Baytullāh because Quraysh are addressed; the plural marks it as the direction joining all mosques and also states a general rule, as in 9:17.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p518/r5.anchor: there is a strong indication that it refers to the Baytull āh. It is signified by a plural word

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r1.claim: They open the hamza of وأن المساجد, linking the clause to the earlier report of listening and making it part of the revelation; Ibn Hurmuz and Talha read it with kasra as a new sentence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وأن المساجد، بفتح الهمزة عطفا على أنه استمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r2.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r2.claim: He understands وأن المساجد لله as the reason for the command not to invoke anyone alongside God in mosques; the apparent meaning is prayer houses dedicated to worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r2.anchor: معنى الآية: وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا: أي لهذا السبب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r3.claim: He says every place where someone prostrates is a mosque, since the whole earth is a mosque for this community; more remote views identify prostration limbs or the Sacred Mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: كل موضع سجد فيه فهو مسجد، كان مخصوصا لذلك أو لم يكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r4.claim: One report says the verse came when Quraysh controlled the Kaaba, to affirm that every place belongs to God and He can be worshiped anywhere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r4.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت حين تغلبت قريش على الكعبة، فقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r5.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r5.claim: He says jinn asked how they could pray with Muhammad from far away, so the verse assured them their worship was accepted wherever they were.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: نزلت لأن الجن قالت: يا رسول الله، كيف نشهد الصلاة معك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r15.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r15.claim: Sibawayh says that when أن المساجد begins with a fatḥa, it coordinates with 1:1, قل أوحي إلي أنه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r15.anchor: ومن فتح الألف من أن المساجد لله جعلها عطفا على قوله قل أوحي إلي أنه [الجن: 1] ، ذكره سيبويه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r16.claim: Some say المساجد means the houses devoted to worship and prayer in every religious community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p382#2/r16.anchor: والمساجد قيل أراد بها البيوت التي هي للعبادة والصلاة في كل ملة

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r3.claim: Worldly work in mosques is disliked; scholars differ on judicial work, which Abu Hanifa permits as religious business while al-Shafiʿi regards it as disliked.
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r3.anchor: واختلفوا في القضاء، لا يكره عند أبي حنيفة؛ لأنها من أمور الدين، وقال الشافعي: يكره

MUQATIL:72:15-23/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r4.claim: Mosques includes churches, synagogues, and mosques; because Jews and Christians associate partners in prayer there, believers are commanded to worship God alone.
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r4.anchor: { وأن المساجد لله } يعني الكنائس والبيع والمساجد لله { فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا }

TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r1.claim: When asked by al-Muʿtasim where a thief's hand is cut, Abu Jaʿfar says to cut at the finger joints and leave the palm, since the palm is needed for prostration; he interprets the seven prostrating limbs as God's mosques, which may not be cut.
TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أنه سأله المعتصم عن السارق من أي موضع يجب أن يقطع

TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq counts eight bones used in prostration, but says seven are obligatory under the verse: forehead, palms, knees, and big toes; placing the nose is sunna.
TABATABAI:72:18-28#2/r2.anchor: عن حماد بن عيسى عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث وسجد يعني أبا عبد الله عليه السلام على ثمانية أعظم

THALABI:v10p54/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p54/r1.claim: After this verse was revealed, Muslims entering a mosque would testify to God's oneness and greet the Messenger.
THALABI:v10p54/r1.anchor: وكان المسلمون بعد نزول هذه الآية إذا دخل أحدهم المسجد قال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله والسلام على رسول الله

THALABI:v10p54/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p54/r2.claim: The Prophetic report also forbids gathering up hair or clothing while prostrating.
THALABI:v10p54/r2.anchor: وأطراف القدمين، وأن لا أكف شعرا ولا ثوبا

THALABI:v10p54/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p54/r3.claim: Hasan understands masajid as all places on earth, since the earth was made a place of prayer for the Prophet; Muslims then recited a testimony and greeting upon entering.
THALABI:v10p54/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: أراد بها البقاع كلها وذلك، أن الأرض جعلت للنبي

THALABI:v10p54/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وطلق بن حبيب
THALABI:v10p54/r4.claim: They interpret masajid as the seven bodily parts used in prostration: feet, knees, hands, and face.
THALABI:v10p54/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وطلق بن حبيب: أراد بالمساجد الأعضاء التي يسجد عليها العبد

THALABI:v10p54/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v10p54/r5.claim: Ibn Ata says a person's prostrating limbs should not be humbled to anyone besides their Creator.
THALABI:v10p54/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء: مساجدك أعضاؤك التي أمرت أن تسجد عليها لا تذللها لغير خالقها

THALABI:v10p54/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p54/r6.claim: The Prophet said he was ordered to prostrate on seven bones, identifying the forehead, hands, knees, and toes, without gathering hair or clothing.
THALABI:v10p54/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة: أعظم الجبهة

THALABI:v10p54/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r7.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
THALABI:v10p54/r7.claim: The Prophet said that when a servant prostrates, seven parts prostrate with him.
THALABI:v10p54/r7.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب، أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إذا سجد العبد سجد معه سبعة»

THALABI:v10p54/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p54/r8.claim: If masajid means places, the singular is masjid with kasra on jīm; if it means bodily parts, it is masjad with fatḥa.
THALABI:v10p54/r8.anchor: فإن جعلت المساجد المواضع فواحدها مسجد بكسر الجيم، وإن جعلت الأعضاء فواحدها مسجد بفتح الجيم

THALABI:v10p54/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p54/r9.claim: Hasan also interprets masajid as prayers, requiring exclusive worship of God; another explanation reserves mosques for worship rather than trade, meetings, roads, or other purposes.
THALABI:v10p54/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: وأن المساجد لله يعني الصلوات فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا أي أفردوا له التوحيد

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r14.claim: The clauses in verses 16 and 18 are direct revelation and are read with fatha unanimously.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r14.anchor: وَاَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقَامُوا [el-Cin 72/16], وَأَنَّ ٱلْمَسَٰجِدَ لِلَّهِ [el-Cin 72/18]

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r16.claim: Elmalılı renders the clauses with doğrusu, hakikat, and fi’l-hakīka, and says they explain rushd as the reasonable, right path.
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r16.anchor: Biz bunları mealde “doğrusu” ve “hakikat” ve “fi’l-hakīka” tâbirleriyle göstermeye çalıştık ve bütün bunlarda rüşdün, mâkul ve doğru yolun bir îzâhı vardır.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r6.claim: The clause is read with fatḥ in every reading and connected to the preceding conditional clause; mosques belong to God, so worship is for God alone.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r6.anchor: Bu da kıraatlerin hepsinde meftuhtur. اَنْ لَو gibi yukarıya ma‘tuftur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r7.claim: Mesâcid is normally the plural of mescid, though it can also be the plural of mesced with fatḥ on the jīm.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r7.anchor: “Mesâcid” mâlum olduğu üzere “mescid”in cem‘idir. Cîm’in fethiyle “mesced”in cem‘i de olur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r8.claim: With kasra, mescid means a place designated for prostration, prayer, and worship; lexically it covers every community’s worship place, while conventionally it means a Muslim mosque.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r8.anchor: olan yerlerdir ki lügaten müslim ve gayr-i müslim her milletin mâbedine şâmil olabilir. Örfte ehl-i islâmın mâbedine mahsustur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r9.claim: The kasra form is an exceptional place-noun pattern that distinguishes a mosque from the regular morphological pattern.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r9.anchor: İmtiyâzına tenbih için ism-i mekânın şâz vezinlerinden olmak üzere meksur okunarak kıyastan ayırt edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r10.claim: With fatḥ, mesced can be a verbal noun for prostration, or a regular place noun for the place or bodily part of prostration.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r10.anchor: Cîm’in fethiyle “mesced” ise secde mânasına mimli masdar veya secde mevzii, secde uzvu mânasına

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r11.claim: Elmalılı cites a Prophetic report that he was commanded to prostrate on seven limbs, which he identifies as forehead and nose, hands, knees, and feet.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r11.anchor: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ عَلَى سَبـْعَةِ آرَابٍ “Yedi a‘zâ üzerine secde ile emr olundum”[^29] hadîsinde beyan olunduğu üzere

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r12.claim: The apparent and majority interpretation is worship places generally, as in 2:114; Jews and Christians also invoke others in synagogues and churches, so Muslims are commanded to worship sincerely.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r12.anchor: burada da zâhir olan evvelki mâna ile ibadethânelerdir, cumhûrun kavli de budur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r13.claim: Because Muslim-specific mosques had not yet been built when this surah was revealed, Elmalılı also considers broader interpretations of mesâcid.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r13.anchor: Ancak bu sûre nâzil olduğu zaman Müslümanlara mahsus mescidler yapılmış olmadığı için

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r14.claim: A Prophetic report says the whole earth was made a mosque and purifier; Hasan al-Basri uses it to support a broad reading.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r15.speaker: حسن البصري
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r15.claim: Hasan al-Basri takes mesâcid to mean all regions of the earth: since the earth belongs to its Creator, no one should prostrate on it to another.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r15.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî demiştir ki: “Burada ‘mesâcid’[^31], Arz’ın bütün buk‘alarına işarettir.”

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r16.claim: Another reading takes mesced as the verbal noun for prostrations, meaning that prayers belong to God and one must not prostrate to anyone else.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r16.anchor: Yahut “mesced” feth ile mimli masdar olmak üzere “secdeler, yani namazlar Allah’a mahsustur; başkasına secde etmeyin” demektir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r17.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the prostrating limbs are God’s creatures, so they must not be used to prostrate to anyone besides God.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r17.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr de demiştir ki: “Secde a‘zâları olan mescedler Allah’ındır, yani Allah’ın mahlûkudur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r18.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Ata, identifies mesâcid here specifically as the Sacred Mosque; because it contains many mosques, other mosques are covered by implication.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r18.anchor: Atâ, İbn Abbas’tan burada “mesâcid”den[^33] murad Mescid-i Haram’dır diye de bir rivayet söylemiştir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r19.claim: Although each interpretation has a rationale, Elmalılı considers the majority’s general meaning, all houses of worship, the most apparent.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r19.anchor: en zâhir olan cumhûr-i ulemânın dediği vechile ale’l-umûm ibadethaneler demek olmasıdır.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r9.speaker: سعي بن جبير وطلق بن حبيب
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r9.claim: Mosques may mean prostration sites in the outer world, the earth, and the inner world, the body.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r9.anchor: مواضع السجود من العالم الآفاقي من الأرض ومن العالم النفسي من الجسد - كما قاله سعي بن جبير وطلق بن حبيب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r10.claim: Because all prostration places belong exclusively to God, creatures must not invoke anyone alongside Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r10.anchor: أي مواضع السجود من العالم الآفاقي من الأرض ومن العالم النفسي من الجسد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r11.claim: Invoking another in God's world with body parts and senses God created is especially blameworthy, since earth, sky, and body are His gifts.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r11.anchor: من تعبد لغير سيده في ملك سيده الذي هو العالم الآفاقي وبآلة سيده الذي هو العالم النفسي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r12.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r12.claim: Al-Baghawi says masjid has kasra on the jīm for prayer places and fatḥa for body parts.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p193/r12.anchor: فإن جعلت المساجد مواضع الصلاة فواحدها بكسر الجيم , وإن جعلتها الأعضاء فواحدها فتح الجيم

FARRA:v3p191/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p191/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p191/r8.claim: A reader who kasra-s the whole passage but puts «وأن المساجد لله» in the accusative ties that phrase specifically to revelation and supplies the oath with «أن لو».
FARRA:v3p191/r8.anchor: ومن كسر كلها ونصب: «وأن المساجد لله» خصه بالوحي، وجعل: وأن لو مضمرة فيها [اليمين على ما وصفت لك

FARRA:v3p193/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p193/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p193/r12.claim: Belonging to God, the mosques must be kept free of idols and anything else worshipped alongside Him.
FARRA:v3p193/r12.anchor: فلا تشركوا فيها صنما ولا شيئا مما يعبد

FARRA:v3p193/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p193/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p193/r13.claim: An alternative explanation takes «mosques» as the body parts used in prostration: forehead, hands, knees, and fronts of the feet.
FARRA:v3p193/r13.anchor: يريد: مساجد الرجل: ما يسجد عليه من: جبهته، ويديه، وركبتيه، وصدور قدميه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r4.claim: Masājid means the places where people pray.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r4.anchor: وأن المساجد لله } يعني: المواضع التي يصلى فيها.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r5.claim: An alternative says masājid means the bodily parts on which people prostrate.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r6.claim: Another alternative takes masājid as prostrations, using the plural of masjid for prostration itself.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r6.anchor: وقيل: يعني: إن السجدات لله، جمع مسجد بمعنى السجود

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r7.claim: The command not to invoke anyone alongside God requires worshipping God alone in prayer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r7.anchor: فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا } أمر بالتوحيد لله تعالى في الصلاة.

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.claim: One reading pattern gives fatḥ to clauses that belong to revelation and kasr to the jinn’s speech; the final clauses about mosques and the Prophet’s standing are exceptions to the jinn’s speech.

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.claim: One parsing is “It was revealed to me that the mosques belong to God.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.anchor: التقدير : قل أوحي إلي أن المساجد لله

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl supplies an omitted lām: “because the mosques belong to God, do not invoke anyone with Him”; the prohibition applies in mosques, which belong exclusively to God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.anchor: ومذهب الخليل أن التقدير : ولأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r3.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r3.claim: Most interpreters take mosques as places built for prayer and remembrance, including synagogues, churches, and Muslim mosques; because People of the Book associate partners in their worship there, Muslims are commanded to worship sincerely and affirm God’s oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول الأكثرين : أنها المواضع التي بنيت للصلاة وذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan also interprets mosques as all places on earth, citing the Prophet’s statement that the earth was made a place of prostration; the earth belongs to God, so one should not prostrate on it to another.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r4.anchor: قال الحسن : أراد بالمساجد البقاع كلها

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan gives another interpretation: mosques are the prayers, with masājid as the plural of masjid, a verbal noun meaning prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r5.anchor: روي عن الحسن أيضا أنه قال : المساجد هي الصلوات

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says mosques are the seven bodily members used in prostration: the feet, knees, hands, and face; they belong to God and should not be used to prostrate to another.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : المساجد الأعضاء التي يسجد العبد عليها

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī selects Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s interpretation of mosques as the body parts on which one prostrates.

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r8.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the mosques mean Mecca with all its mosques, since it is the world’s qibla and everyone turns toward it in prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r8.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يريد بالمساجد مكة

RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r9.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r9.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the singular is masjid with fatḥ in all interpretations except purpose-built prayer places, whose singular has kasr; he lists المسجد، المطلع، المنسك، المسكن، المنبت، المفرق، المسقط، المجزر، المحشر، المشرق، المغرب as exceptions, though fatḥ is permissible in all.
RAZI-FULL:v30p143#2/r9.anchor: وواحد المساجد على الأقوال كلها مسجد بفتح

RAZI-FULL:v30p144/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v30p144/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it is sunna for a man entering a mosque to say “There is no god but God,” since the prohibition on invoking anyone with God implicitly commands remembering and calling upon Him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144/r1.anchor: قال الحسن : من السنة إذا دخل الرجل المسجد أن يقول لا إله إلا الله

STUDYQURAN:72:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r1.claim: Masājid is plural of both masjid, a place of prostration, and masjad, an instrument of prostration.
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r1.anchor: Places of worship translates masājid, the plural form of both masjid

STUDYQURAN:72:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r2.claim: Masjid is Muslims’ standard word for mosque; English derives from it, and most occurrences are translated mosque.
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r2.anchor: standard word used by Muslims for “mosque,” from which this English word

STUDYQURAN:72:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r3.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r3.claim: One interpretation takes the places of worship to mean all religious communities’ houses of worship.
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r3.anchor: here is taken as a reference to all houses of worship for all religions

STUDYQURAN:72:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the plural to refer to the whole earth, supported by the Prophet’s saying that it was made a purified place of prostration for him.
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r4.anchor: all houses of worship for all religions (Bg) or to the whole of the

STUDYQURAN:72:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r5.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r5.claim: The Prophet said the earth was made a place of prostration for him and purified.
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r5.anchor: earth (Bg, Q, Ṭ) in accordance with a famous saying of the Prophet: “The earth

STUDYQURAN:72:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r6.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r6.claim: If masājid is plural of masjad, it refers to the seven body parts touching the ground in Muslim prayer prostration: forehead, hands, feet, and knees.
STUDYQURAN:72:18/r6.anchor: If taken as the plural for masjad, it refers to the seven parts of the body that should all touch the ground

TAB-FULL:v23p341/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r1.claim: God commands people not to associate anything with Him in mosques, but to devote worship and exclusive unity to Him.
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r1.anchor: تشركوا به فيها شيئا، ولكن أفردوا له التوحيد، وأخلصوا له العبادة

TAB-FULL:v23p341/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r2.claim: Qatāda says Jews and Christians associated partners with God in their churches and synagogues, so the Prophet was commanded to worship God alone.
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا} [الجن: 18] كانت اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا كنائسهم وبيعهم أشركوا بالله

TAB-FULL:v23p341/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that the jinn asked how they could attend the mosque and pray with the Prophet from far away; this verse was revealed in response.
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، {وأن المساجد لله} [الجن: 18] قال: قالت الجن لنبي الله: كيف لنا نأتي المسجد، ونحن ناءون عنك

TAB-FULL:v23p341/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says al-masājid means all mosques.
TAB-FULL:v23p341/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة ، {وأن المساجد لله} [الجن: 18] قال: المساجد كلها

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.claim: The verses derive the Prophet’s mission, divine oneness, and resurrection from the jinn story, then close by indicating the messenger’s protection from error.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.anchor: في الآيات تسجيل للنبوة وذكر وحدانيته تعالى والمعاد كالاستنتاج من القصة وتختتم بالإشارة إلى عصمة الرسالة

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r2.claim: The clause is conjoined to ‘they listened’; God’s ownership of mosques explains the command not to invoke another with Him.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r2.anchor: معطوف على قوله { أنه استمع } الخ، وجملة { أن المساجد لله } في موضع التعليل لقوله { فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا }

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r3.claim: Here duʿāʾ means worship; God also names worship duʿāʾ in 40:60.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r3.anchor: والمراد بالدعاء العبادة وقد سماها الله دعاء كما في قوله

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r4.claim: Some identify al-masājid as the Kaʿba, the Sacred Mosque, or the Sacred Mosque together with Jerusalem; the author rejects these because a plural does not fit one or two places.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r4.anchor: وقد اختلف في المراد من المساجد فقيل المراد به الكعبة، وقيل المسجد الحرام،

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r5.claim: The view that al-masājid means the sanctuary is unsupported and, the author says, a taunt.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r5.anchor: وقيل الحرم، وهو تهكم لا دليل عليه

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r6.claim: One interpretation takes al-masājid as the whole earth, citing the Prophet’s saying that the earth was made a place of prayer and a purifier.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r6.anchor: وقيل الأرض كلها لقوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r7.claim: That hadith establishes only that worship is permitted anywhere, unlike Jewish and Christian restrictions to synagogues and churches; it does not establish that every place is ordinarily called a mosque.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r7.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يدل على أزيد من جواز العبادة في أي بقعة من بقاع الأرض خلافا لما هو المعروف عن اليهود والنصارى

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r8.claim: Another view takes al-masājid as the prayers and interprets the verse as prayer only to God; the author calls it unsupported and a taunt.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد به الصلوات فلا يصلى إلا لله، وهو تهكم لا دليل عليه

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r9.speaker: الإمام الجواد عليه السلام
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r9.claim: Imam al-Jawad says the mosques are the seven bodily members placed on the ground in prostration: forehead, palms, knees, and toes.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r9.anchor: وعن الإمام الجواد عليه السلام أن المراد بالمساجد الأعضاء السبعة التي يسجد عليها في الصلاة وهي الجبهة والكفان والركبتان

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والفراء والزجاج
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r10.claim: The body-members interpretation is also transmitted from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Farraʾ, and al-Zajjaj.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r10.anchor: ونقل ذلك أيضا عن سعيد بن جبير والفراء والزجاج

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r11.claim: On the body-members reading, those prostration sites belong to God by religious designation; duʿāʾ here is prostration as worship’s clearest instance, or prayer because it includes prostration.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r11.anchor: والأنسب على هذا أن يكون المراد بكون مواضع السجود من الإنسان لله اختصاصها به اختصاصا تشريعيا

BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r12.claim: The clause is another item revealed, coordinated with the opening revelation that the jinn listened; the mosques belong to God for worship, especially the Sacred Mosque, hence Bayt Allah.
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r12.anchor: عطف على قوله إنه استمتع أي وأوحى إلى إن المساجد مختصة بالله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r13.claim: Mosques include places built for prayer and remembrance, including the worship houses of other religious communities such as churches and synagogues.
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r13.anchor: فالمراد بالمساجد المواضع التي بنيت للصلاة وذكر الله

BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r14.claim: Attributing a mosque to a person or place does not contradict its belonging to God: such names may indicate its builder or location.
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r14.anchor: ثم هذا لا ينافي أن تضاف المساجد وتنسب إلى غيره تعالى بوجه آخر إما لبانيها كمسجد رسول الله أو لمكانها

BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r15.claim: The hierarchy of sanctity runs from the Sacred Mosque to the Prophet's Mosque, Jerusalem, congregational mosques, neighborhood mosques, street mosques, and home mosques.
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r15.anchor: وأعظم المساجد حرمة المسجد الحرام ثم مسجد المدينة ثم مسجد بيت القمدس

BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r16.claim: The causal fa prohibits worshipping anyone alongside God in mosques; if associating partners is blameworthy, directing worship exclusively to another is worse.
BURSEVI:v10p151#2/r16.anchor: أي لا تعبدوا فيها الفاء للسببية

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r1.claim: The mosques of the heart should be purified for the manifestation of God's Greatest Name alone, with no partial names beside it.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r1.anchor: فلا تدعوا مع الله أحا من الأسماء الجزئية أي طهروا مساجد قلوبكم لتجلي اسم الله الأعظم فيها لا غير

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata calls the mosques the body's prostrating limbs—face, hands, knees, and feet—and says they must not be humbled before anything but their Creator.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء مساجدك أعضاؤك التي أمرت أن تسجد عليها لا تخضعها ولا تذللها لغير خالقه

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r3.claim: These limbs drive movement and action, through which sins and desires are pursued; prostrating with them atones, erases sin, and purifies.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r3.anchor: إن هذه الأعضاء التي عليها مدار الحركة هي المفاصل التي تنفتح وتنطبق في المشي والبطش وأكثر السعي

TABRISI:72:1#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:72:1#2/r3.claim: Sibawayh says exegetes attach the mosques clause to “it was revealed to me”: it was revealed that the mosques belong to God.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r3.anchor: زعم سيبويه أن المفسرين حملوه على أوحي كأنه وأوحي إلي أن المساجد لله

TABRISI:72:1#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:72:1#2/r4.claim: Al-Khalil instead supplies a causal “because”: because mosques belong to God, invoke no one alongside Him.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r4.anchor: ومذهب الخليل أنه على قوله ولأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا

TABRISI:72:1#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r5.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:72:1#2/r5.claim: Al-Khalil compares this construction with “because your community is one” in 23:52 and “for this, worship Me” in 21:92, and with the construction in Sūrat Quraysh.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r5.anchor: كما أن قوله وأن هذه أمتكم

TABRISI:72:1#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r6.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:72:1#2/r6.claim: Sibawayh says reading wa-inna al-masājid with kasr would also be good.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه: ولو قرأ وإن المساجد بالكسر لكان جيدا

TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.claim: After quoted speech and a conditional faʾ, the following clause can begin independently with an omitted introduction; Sibawayh applies this to examples including 72:23.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.anchor: وكذلك ما بعد فاء الجزاء لأن ما بعد فاء الجزاء موضع ابتداء

TABRISI:72:17-18/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r13.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:72:17-18/r13.claim: Al-Khalil’s construction means: because mosques belong to God, invoke no one besides Him in them.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r13.anchor: تقديره ولأن المسجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا سوى الله عن الخليل

TABRISI:72:17-18/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:17-18/r14.claim: The command forbids invoking anyone alongside God in places built for prayer, as Christians do in churches and polytheists do at the Kaʿba.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r14.anchor: لا تذكروا مع الله في المواضع التي بنيت للعبادة والصلاة أحدا على وجه الإشراك

TABRISI:72:17-18/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r15.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:72:17-18/r15.claim: Al-Hasan says it is Sunnah on entering mosques to declare that there is no god but God and that one invokes no one alongside Him.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r15.anchor: قال الحسن: من السنة عند دخول المساجد أن يقال لا إله إلا الله

TABRISI:72:17-18/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r16.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والزجاج والفراء
TABRISI:72:17-18/r16.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Zajjaj, and al-Farraʾ take “mosques” as the seven body parts used in prostration, which belong to God and should prostrate to no one else.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r16.anchor: وقيل: المساجد مواضع السجود من الإنسان وهي الجبهة والكفان

TABRISI:72:17-18/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر بن علي بن موسى الرضا
TABRISI:72:17-18/r17.claim: When al-Muʿtaṣim asked, Abu Jaʿfar ibn ʿAli ibn Musa al-Riḍā answered that the mosques are the seven body parts on which one prostrates.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r17.anchor: وروي أن المعتصم سأل أبا جعفر بن علي بن موسى الرضا ع عن قوله

TABRISI:72:17-18/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r18.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:72:17-18/r18.claim: Another view from al-Hasan takes the mosques as all regions of the earth, which God made a place of prayer for Muhammad.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r18.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد بالمساجد البقاع كلها وذلك لأن الأرض كلها جعلت

TABRISI:72:17-18/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r19.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:72:17-18/r19.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that the jinn asked how they could reach the mosque and pray with the Prophet from far away, and the verse was revealed.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r19.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: قالت الجن للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: كيف لنا أن نأتي المسجد

TABRISI:72:17-18/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:17-18/r20.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:72:17-18/r20.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets mosques as the prayers themselves: worship should be devoted to God alone, with no share given to another.
TABRISI:72:17-18/r20.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أيضا أن المساجد الصلوات وهي لله والمراد أخلصوا لله العبادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r1.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r1.claim: Sibawayh links the clause to “it was revealed to me”: it was revealed that the mosques belong to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r1.anchor: زعم سيبويه أن المفسرين حملوه على "أوحي" كأنه أوحي إلي أن المساجد لله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r2.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r2.claim: Al-Khalil takes it as a causal clause: because the mosques belong to God, invoke no one besides Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r3.claim: The causal construction is compared to 21:92: because the community is one and God is its Lord, it should worship Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r3.anchor: كما أن قوله: {إن هذه أمتكم} [الأنبياء: 92]، على معنى: ولأن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاعبدون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r4.claim: Most commentators say the mosques are places built for prayer and remembrance of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r4.anchor: على أنها المواضع التي بنيت للصلاة وذكر الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r5.claim: Muqatil includes churches, synagogues, and Muslim mosques.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني الكنائس، والبيع، ومساجد المسلمين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r6.claim: The command means not to worship anyone alongside God; the People of the Book associated partners at their churches and synagogues, so believers must make their invocation exclusive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r6.anchor: فلا تعبدوا مع الله أحدا، وذلك أن أهل الكتاب يشركون في صلاتهم في البيع، والكنائس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r7.claim: Qatada similarly says Jews and Christians associated partners when entering their places of worship, so God commanded sincere invocation in the mosque.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت اليهود والنصارى، إذا دخلوا كنائسهم، وبيعهم أشركوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r8.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the report from ʿIkrima, says the phrase means all mosques.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r8.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة قال: المساجد كلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r9.claim: On the place-of-prostration interpretation, masjid may have fatḥa on jīm for the place on the ground or kasra as a collective name for a place of prostration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r9.anchor: واحدها يجوز أن يكون مسجدا -بفتح الجيم-، وهو موضع السجود من الأرض، ويجوز أن يكون مسجدا -بكسر الجيم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r10.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the mosques are the seven bodily parts used in prostration: feet, knees, hands, and face.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r10.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: المساجد: الأعضاء التي يسجد عليها العبد، وهي سبعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbari prefers the bodily-parts interpretation: since God originated these limbs, one should not prostrate on them to another, thereby denying His favor.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r12.claim: On the bodily-parts reading, the singular masjid has fatḥa on jīm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r12.anchor: معنى المساجد: مواضع السجود من الجسد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r13.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r13.claim: Al-Hasan understands the word as all regions of the earth, all of which are places where this community may prostrate and were made a mosque for it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r13.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال: أراد البقاع كلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r14.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r14.claim: On al-Hasan’s view, the earth is God’s creation, so people should not prostrate on it to anyone other than its Creator.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p315/r14.anchor: وهي كلها جعلت مسجدا لهذه الأمة، يقول: الأرض كلها مخلوقة لله، فلا يسجدوا عليها لغير خالقها

QASHANI:72:18-21/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:18-21/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:18-21/r1.claim: Mosques signify each faculty's perfection as its submission to the heart, or the perfection of anything, including heart and spirit; belonging to God is His due or manifested attribute there.
QASHANI:72:18-21/r1.anchor: مقام كمال كل قوة هو هيئة إذعانها وانقيادها للقلب الذي هو سجودها

QASHANI:72:18-21/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:18-21/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:18-21/r2.claim: Calling on another with God means pursuing egoic goals, caprice, pleasures, and desires according to one's nature, thereby associating with God.
QASHANI:72:18-21/r2.anchor: بتحصيل أغراض النفس وعبادة الهوى وطلب اللذات والشهوات

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r1.claim: A masjid is a place set aside for Muslims’ prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r1.anchor: Mescid, müslümanların namaz kılmalarına ayrılmış mekânı ifade eder (bk. Bakara 2/114).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r2.claim: The verse links back to the jinn listening in verse 1 and teaches that places of worship belong to God, so people must worship no one else.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r2.anchor: Bu âyet de sûrenin birinci âyetinde geçen, “bir cin topluluğunun (Kur’an’ı) dinlediği” meâlindeki cümlecikle bağlantılı olup ibadet yerlerinin Allah’a mahsus olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur takes al-masājid to mean the Sacred Mosque; the verse warns polytheists who placed idols in the Kaaba and worshipped them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r3.anchor: Âyet Kâbe’ye putları yerleştirip onlara tapan müşrikleri uyarmakta ve yaptıklarının yanlış olduğuna işaret etmektedir (İbn Âşûr, XXIX, 240).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the word to mean the whole earth, since prayer and worship are not confined to mosques.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r4.anchor: Namaz ve ibadet yalnız camilere hasredilmiş olmadığından burada bütün yeryüzü kastedilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r5.claim: Some interpret the word as the body parts touching the ground in prostration—hands, feet, knees, and forehead—and infer that these should prostrate only to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r5.anchor: Secdede yere temas eden uzuvlar yani eller, ayaklar, dizler ve alın kastedilmiş, Allah’ın verdiği bu organlarla O’ndan başkasına secde edilmemesi emredilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r6.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r6.claim: Some exegetes read the term as prayer itself, since prostration is one of prayer’s pillars.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:18/r6.anchor: Bazı müfessirlerce, secdenin namazın bir rüknü olduğu göz önüne alınarak bu kelime “namaz” anlamıyla da açıklanmıştır (Şevkânî, V, 356).

SULAMI:v2p353#7/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p353#7/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p353#7/r1.claim: No one shares in God’s house so as to bar His servants from calling upon Him; likewise, none may prevent what belongs to God in this respect.
SULAMI:v2p353#7/r1.anchor: قال سهل : لا يدع مع الله شريكا أي ليس لأحد معي شركة في بيتي أن يمنع عبادي عن دعوتي

SULAMI:v2p353#7/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p353#7/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p353#7/r2.claim: The mosques are the body parts on which one is commanded to prostrate; do not humble or abase them to anyone besides their Creator.
SULAMI:v2p353#7/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : مساجدك اعضاؤك التي امرت أن تسجد عليها لا تخضعها ولا تذلها لغير خالقها

TUSTARI:72:18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:72:18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:72:18/r1.claim: Do not call on a partner with God: none can prevent His servants from remembering Him, and what belongs to God cannot be barred or restrained by anyone.
TUSTARI:72:18/r1.anchor: أي لا تدعوا مع الله شريكا، أي ليس لأحد معي شريك في شيء يمنع عبادي من ذكري

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the jinn asked permission to attend prayers with the Prophet in his mosque, and this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالت الجن يا رسول الله ائذن لنا أن نشهد معك الصلوات في مسجدك

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr gives a similar report: the jinn asked how they could attend the mosque and prayer while far from the Prophet, prompting the verse.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p222/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال قالت الجن للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف لنا أن نأتي المسجد ونحن ناءون عنك

DAMGHANI:v1p231/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r8.claim: Masājid can mean the bodily parts used in prostration: forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r8.anchor: السادس : المساجد أعضاء السجود قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

FARRA:v3p190/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p190/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v3p190/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says this clause was revealed to Muhammad after the account of the jinn.
FARRA:v3p190/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أوحي إلى النبي- صلى الله عليه وسلم- بعد اقتصاص أمر الجن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#2/r1.claim: Al-masājid means prostration to God; masjid is a verbal noun alongside sujūd, like maḍrab alongside ḍarb, and its plural is masājid.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r10.claim: An is accusative and coordinated with the preceding clause; al-masājid is the plural of masjid, as illustrated by maḍrib.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r10.anchor: بنصب (أن) نسق على ما تقدم من قوله: يريد أن السجود لله، ولا يكون لغيره، جمع مسجد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r11.claim: Prostration belongs to God and must not be directed to anyone else.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r11.anchor: يريد أن السجود لله، ولا يكون لغيره، جمع مسجد

NAHHAS:v5p50/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p50/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p50/r11.claim: أن is accusative with understood لِـ (‘because’); another analysis makes it nominative, coordinated with أنه in قل أوحي إلي.
NAHHAS:v5p50/r11.anchor: أن في موضع نصب بمعنى ولأن وعلى قول بعضهم في موضع رفع

NAHHAS:v5p50/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p50/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p50/r12.claim: The prohibition addresses a group; jussive mood deletes its nūn.
NAHHAS:v5p50/r12.anchor: ( فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا ) نهي لجماعة وحذفت منه النون للجزم

SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r1.speaker: السبعة
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r1.claim: The seven readers agree on فتح أن; it either omits a preposition and attaches to فلا تدعوا, as al-Khalīl analyzes, or coordinates with أنه استمع as another revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r1.anchor: قد تقدم أن السبعة أجمعت على الفتح، وأن فيه وجهين: حذف الجار ويتعلق بقوله: " فلا تدعوا "

SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r2.speaker: ابن هرمز وطلحة
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r2.claim: Ibn Hurmuz and Ṭalḥa read وإن المساجد with kasra, allowing an independent clause or a causal reading equivalent to al-Khalīl's.
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز. وطلحة " وإن المساجد " بالكسر، وهو محتمل للاستئناف وللتعليل

SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r3.claim: المساجد may be plural of masjid with kasra, the place of prostration; or of masjid with fatḥ for prostrating body parts; or plural of the verbal noun for types of prostration.
SAMIN-DURR:72:18/r3.anchor: والمساجد قيل: هي جمع " مسجد " بالكسر وهو موضع السجود، وتقدم أن قياسه الفتح

ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r6.claim: The command is to worship God alone in the prayers.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r6.anchor: معناه الأمر بتوحيد الله في الصلوات

ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r7.claim: One interpretation takes al-masājid as the human body's prostration points: forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r7.anchor: وقيل المساجد مواضع السجود من الإنسان، الجبهة والأنف

ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r8.claim: The clause introduced by an can be accusative or genitive: it means because the mosques belong to God, with an omitted lām yielding the accusative, or genitive by Arab usage without an expressed lām.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r8.anchor: و" أن " ههنا يصلح أن يكون في موضع نصب ويصلح أن يكون في موضع جر

ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r9.claim: The omitted-preposition genitive has an Arabic parallel in the expression wa-baladin laysa bihi anīs, meaning rubba balad.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جرا وإن لم تظهر اللام، كما تقول العرب: وبلد ليس به أنيس

ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r1.claim: All worship belongs to God alone, so no one else is to be invoked alongside Him.
ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r1.anchor: all worship [14] is due to God [alone]: hence, do not invoke anyone side by side with God

ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n14/r1.claim: Al-masajid literally means places of worship, and here denotes worship as such.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza in four clauses; Nafi and Abu Bakr's Asim transmission agree except they kasra وإنه لما at 72:19, while Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai open all except after speech or a jawab فاء; Hafs matches Hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: قل أوحي إلي أنه [1]، وأن لو استقاموا [16] وأن المساجد لله [18]، وأنه لما قام عبد الله [19] أربعة أحرف بالفتح

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r6.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r6.claim: Sibawayh connects وأن المساجد لله to أوحي, supplying the sense that it was revealed the mosques belong to God.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r6.anchor: فزعم سيبويه أن المفسرين حملوه على: أوحي* كأنه: وأوحي إلي أن المساجد لله

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r7.speaker: الخليل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r7.claim: Al-Khalil instead links the clause to لأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا, as with the purpose construction in the cited passage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r7.anchor: ومذهب الخليل أنه على قوله: ولأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا، كما أن قوله: أن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r1.speaker: الخليل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r1.claim: Al-Khalil's ellipsis analysis supplies لهذا فاعبدوني, paralleling his reading of لإيلاف قريش as لهذا فليعبدوا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r1.anchor: أي: لهذا فاعبدوني، ومثله في قول الخليل: لإيلاف قريش [قريش/ 1] كأنه: لهذا فليعبدوا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r2.claim: Mosques may mean houses of worship where idols must not be associated with God, or places where worshippers prostrate.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r2.anchor: فأما المساجد فقيل فيها: إنها بيوت العبادة، أي: لا تشركوا فيها الأوثان مع الله في العبادة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r3.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r3.claim: Sibawayh says the alternative reading وإن المساجد لله would also be good Arabic.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p332/r3.anchor: فقال سيبويه: ولو قرئ: وإن المساجد لله لكان جيدا.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.claim: These four instances of an vary between fatḥa, coordinated with “it was revealed to me,” and kasra, coordinated with “they said: we heard”; after fa in a conditional response, kasra alone is used.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.anchor: هذه الأربعة تقرأ بالفتح وباقي ما قبلها بالكسر فالفتح بالعطف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza in all four cited clauses.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ﴿ قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع ﴾ ﴿ وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.speaker: عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع، والمفضل عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim and Nafi match Abu Amr except that both read the hamza in وأنه لما قام عبد الله with kasra; al-Mufaddal transmits the same from Asim.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع كما قرأ أبو عمرو

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.claim: These readers open the hamza except where the clause follows a statement or a fāʾ of recompense.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم كل ذلك بالفتح إلا ما جاء بعد قول أو بعد فاء جزاء

NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.claim: All agree on fatḥa in annahu istamaʿa and an al-masājidu lillāh because these cannot be the jinn's speech but are revelation; the remaining cases could be either their speech or revelation.
NASHR:v2p391#2/r3.anchor: واتفقوا على فتح أنه استمع، وأن المساجد لله لأنه لا يصح أن يكون من قولهم، بل هو مما أوحي إليه

NASHR:v2p126/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p126/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p126/r1.claim: Reciters treat rawm as part of a vowel, so they bar it on non-nunated fatḥa; grammarians treat it as hidden movement and permit it on all three vowels, as in an yaḍriba.
NASHR:v2p126/r1.anchor: فعلى قول القراء لا يدخل على حركة الفتح لأن الفتحة خفيفة فإذا خرج بعضها خرج سائرها

NASHR:v2p126/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p126/r2.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v2p126/r2.claim: Sībawayh says one performs rawm on accusative or genitive forms but has no recourse to ishmām; this supports the grammarians' broader account of rawm.
NASHR:v2p126/r2.anchor: قال سيبويه في كتابه: أما ما كان في موضع نصب أو جر فإنك تروم فيه الحركة

NASHR:v2p126/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p126/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p126/r3.claim: For reciters, rawm differs from ikhtilās and ikhfaʾ, while ikhtilās and ikhfaʾ mean the same; some writers loosely call rawm ikhfaʾ, and al-Dānī's equation is questionable.
NASHR:v2p126/r3.anchor: فالروم عند القراء غير الاختلاس، وغير الإخفاء أيضا

NASHR:v2p126/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p126/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p126/r4.claim: No rawm or ishmām applies when feminine tāʾ is replaced by hāʾ at pause; if the written tāʾ is retained instead, both are allowed because that consonant normally bears the vowel.
NASHR:v2p126/r4.anchor: أما إذا وقف عليه بالتاء اتباعا لخط المصحف فيما كتب من ذلك بالتاء كما سيأتي في الباب الآتي فإنه يجوز الوقف عليه بالروم

NASHR:v2p126/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p126/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p126/r5.claim: A word ending in an open doubled consonant must be stopped with sukun while keeping the shadda; two consecutive quiescent letters are allowed at pause, and stopping on fatḥa is wrong.
NASHR:v2p126/r5.anchor: يتعين التحفظ في الوقف على المشدد المفتوح بالحركة نحو: صواف، ويحق الحق

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323/r1.claim: Qatāda says Jews and Christians associated partners with God when entering their houses of worship, so the Prophet was commanded to devote his invocation to God when entering the mosque.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا ﴾ قال كانت اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا كنائسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r1.claim: The clause is coordinated with the statement that the jinn listened, so it too belongs to what was revealed; “mosques” most naturally means places prepared for prayer and worship, belonging exclusively to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r1.anchor: عطف على أنه استمع فهو من جملة الموحى والظاهر أن المراد بالمساجد المواضع المعدة للصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes “mosques” to mean every place on earth where someone prostrates, whether or not it was designated for worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن المراد كل موضع سجد فيه من الأرض سواء أعد لذلك أم لا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r3.claim: A sound hadith says that the earth was made a mosque and a purification for the Prophet; al-Ālūsī notes the familiar claim that this is a privilege of his law.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r3.anchor: في الحديث الصحيح جعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وطهورا واشتهر أن هذا من خصائص نبينا صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r4.claim: It is commonly said that prayer on the whole earth, unlike prayer only in synagogues and churches, is a special feature of the Prophet’s community.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r4.anchor: واشتهر أن هذا من خصائص نبينا صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أي شريعته فيكون له ولأمته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r5.claim: An objection to that exclusivity is that Jesus and other prophets travelled; barring prayer outside synagogues and churches would leave them unable to pray often.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r5.anchor: استشكل بأن عيسى عليه السلام كان يكثر السياحة وغيره من الأنبياء عليهم السلام يسافرون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r6.claim: One answer says the distinctive privilege is the combination of the earth as mosque and purification; the special availability of dry ablution suffices to establish the distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r6.anchor: ولذا قيل المخصوص كونها مسجدا وطهورا أي المجموع ويكفي في اختصاصه اختصاص التيمم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r7.claim: Another answer limits the privilege to comparison with earlier communities, not their prophets; if al-Khiḍr lives today, he belongs to this community, prophet or not, under the hadith about Moses following the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r7.anchor: بالنسبة إلى الأمم السالفة دون أنبيائها عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r8.claim: The argument about al-Khiḍr cites the Prophet’s statement that Moses, were he alive, would have to follow him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r8.anchor: لخبر لو كان موسى حيا ما وسعه إلا اتباعي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r9.claim: Another interpretation identifies the mosques as the Sacred Mosque, either the Kaʿba itself or the whole sanctuary; the plural is explained by its sides or by its status as the qibla of mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد بها المسجد الحرام أي الكعبة نفسها أو الحرم كله على ما قيل والجمع لأن كل ناحية منه مسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that when this verse was revealed, the only mosques on earth were the Sacred Mosque and the Jerusalem sanctuary.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس لم يكن يوم نزلت وأن المساجد لله الخ في الأرض مسجدا لا المسجد الحرام ومسجد إيليا بيت المقدس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r11.speaker: ابن عطاء وابن جبير والزجاج والفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn Jubayr, al-Zajjāj, and al-Farrāʾ are cited for taking the term to mean the seven body parts used in prostration: feet, knees, hands, face, forehead, and nose.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء وابن جبير والزجاج والفراء المراد بها قتائدة ثنية معروفة أه منه الأعضاء السبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r12.speaker: المعتصم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r12.claim: Al-Muʿtaṣim asked Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Mūsā about the term, and he answered with the seven body parts.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r12.anchor: وروي أن المعتصم سأل أبا جعفر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r13.claim: A further view takes “mosques” to mean the prostrations themselves, with the word formed as a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r13.anchor: وقيل السجدات على أن المسجد بفتح الجيم مصدر ميمي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r14.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r14.claim: Al-Khalīl reads an implicit causal lām: “because the mosques belong to God”; the verse then directly explains the prohibition on invoking another.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r14.anchor: ونقل عن الخليل بن أحمد أن قوله تعالى وأن المساجد بتقدير لام التعليل وهو متعلق بما بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r15.claim: Because no explicit condition precedes the fāʾ, one analysis treats it as formally extra, with causality already expressed by the implied lām; others hear an implied conditional sense, or take the fāʾ to reinforce or signal that lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r15.anchor: ولما لم تكن الفاء في جواب شرط محقق كانت في الحقيقة زائدة فلا يمتنع تقديم معمول ما بعدها عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r16.claim: The implied sense is that God loves exclusive worship; if people fail to affirm unity everywhere, they must at least not associate partners in mosques, where it is especially abhorrent.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r16.anchor: والمعنى أن الله تعالى يحب أن يوحد ولا يشرك به أحد فإن لم يوحدوه في سائر المواضع فلا تدعوا معه أحدا في المساجد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r17.claim: The construction is compared with the command to worship after God’s favors to Quraysh.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r17.anchor: ونظير هذا قوله تعالى لإيلاف قريش إيلافهم رحلة الشتاء والصيف فليعبدوا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r18.claim: Al-Ālūsī cites Ibn Jubayr for a report that the jinn asked how they could attend prayer with the Prophet while far away; the verse addresses their worship and its acceptance when free of association.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r18.anchor: ليخاطبهم على معنى أن عبادتكم حيث كانت مقبولة إذا لم تشركوا فيها وهو خطاب عام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r19.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r19.claim: Qatāda says Jews and Christians associated partners with God when entering their churches and synagogues, so Muslims were commanded to make their worship sincere in mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r19.anchor: وعن قتادة كان اليهود والنصارة إذا دخلوا كنائسهم ويبعهم أشركوا بالله عز وجل فأمرنا أن نخلص لله تعالى الدعوة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r20.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r20.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the command as an instruction to them to affirm God’s oneness.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r20.anchor: وعن ابن جريج بدل فأمرنا الخ فأمرهم أن يوحدوه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r21.speaker: ابن هرمز وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r21.claim: Ibn Hurmuz and Ṭalḥa read the initial hamza of “inna” with kasra, treating it as a new sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p91/r21.anchor: وقرأ كما في البحر ابن هرمز وطلحة وإن المساجد بكسر همزة إن وحمل ذلك على الاستئناف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r1.claim: Al-masājid means places built for prayer and remembrance of God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r1.anchor: {وأن المساجد لله} يعني المواضع التي بنيت للصلاة وذكر الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r2.claim: Qatada says Jews and Christians associated others with God in churches and synagogues, so believers are commanded to devote invocation to God in every mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا كنائسهم وبيعهم أشركوا بالله فأمر الله المؤمنين أن يخلصوا لله الدعوة إذا دخلوا المساجد وأراد بها المساجد كلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r3.claim: Al-Hasan understands masājid as all places, since the whole earth was made a place of prostration for the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: أراد بها البقاع كلها لأن الأرض جعلت كلها مسجدا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the jinn asked how they could come to the mosque and attend prayer with the Prophet from far away, and this verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: قالت الجن للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف لنا أن [نأتي المسجد وأن] (2) نشهد معك الصلاة ونحن ناءون؟ فنزلت: "وأن المساجد لله"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r5.claim: A second report from Said ibn Jubayr takes masājid as the seven body parts on which a person prostrates.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r5.anchor: وروي عن سعيد بن جبير أيضا: أن المراد بالمساجد الأعضاء التي يسجد عليها الإنسان وهي سبعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r6.claim: On the body-part reading, those limbs are created by God and must not be used to prostrate to anyone else.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r6.anchor: يقول: هذه الأعضاء التي يقع عليها السجود مخلوقة لله فلا تسجدوا عليها لغيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's command to prostrate on seven parts: forehead, hands, knees, and toes, without gathering clothing or hair.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة أعضاء: الجبهة -وأشار بيده إليها -واليدين والركبتين وأطراف القدمين ولا أكف الثوب ولا الشعر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r8.claim: If it means prayer places, masjid has kasra on the jīm; if it means body parts, the jīm has fatḥa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r8.anchor: فإن جعلت المساجد مواضع الصلاة فواحدها مسجد بكسر الجيم، وإن جعلتها الأعضاء فواحدها مسجد بفتح الجيم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r7.claim: Mosques are devoted exclusively to God, so no one else may be worshipped in them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r7.anchor: مختصة به. { فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا } فلا تعبدوا فيها غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r8.claim: Taking an implied lām after “that” as the reason for the prohibition would erase the explanatory value of the fa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r8.anchor: ومن جعل { أن } مقدرة باللام علة للنهي ألغى فائدة الفاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r9.claim: “Mosques” may refer to the whole earth, since it was made a place of prayer for the Prophet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد ب { المسجد } الأرض كلها لأنها جعلت للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام مسجدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r10.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r10.claim: Alternatively, it means the Sacred Mosque; the word may also mean places of prostration, with a prohibition on prostrating to anyone but God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r10.anchor: وقيل المسجد الحرام لأنه قيل المساجد ومواضع السجود على أن المراد النهي عن السجود لغير الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r11.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r11.claim: Alternatively, the plural refers to the body's seven prostration limbs or to prostrations themselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:17-18/r11.anchor: وآرابه السبعة أو السجدات على أنه جمع مسجد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r1.claim: In jītuka annaka, the construction means jītuka li-annaka: the lām is deleted before an; the deleted preposition makes the dependent construction accusative.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r1.anchor: تقول جئتك أنك تريد المعروف إنما أراد جئتك لأنك تريد المعروف ولكنك حذفت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r2.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r2.claim: Khalīl parses Q 23:52 as if it said wa-li-anna hādhihi ummatukum; similarly, deleting the lām from li-īlāfi in Q 106:1 leaves an accusative construction for fa-li-yaʿbudū.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r3.claim: The phrase in Q 23:52 can also be read with inna as a fresh clause, which Sībawayh says is good Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r3.anchor: ولو قلت جئتك إنك تحب المعروف مبتدأ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r4.claim: The annī clauses in Q 23:26 and Q 11:25 are understood as bi-annī; Sībawayh explains them as omitting the preposition bāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r4.anchor: أراد بأني مغلوب ~~وبأني لكم نذير مبين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r5.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r5.claim: Khalīl reads wa-an al-masājida li-llāh as wa-li-an: because the mosques belong to God, worship none with Him; the lām analysis also explains the clause's relation to the governing verb.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r5.anchor: ولأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r6.speaker: المفسرون
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r6.claim: The commentators instead construe wa-an al-masājida as governed by ūḥiya, parallel to wa-annahu lammā qāma ʿabdu llāh yadʿūhu in Q 72:19; reading wa-inna is also possible.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r7.claim: Sībawayh favors Khalīl's lām analysis: its semantic relation to the verb permits fronting or postponing the clause, like other constituents linked through lām.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r7.anchor: المعنى معنى اللام فإذا كان الفعل أو غيره موصلا إليه باللام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r8.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line manaʿtu Tamīman can be read either with an omitted lām or as a fresh inna clause; Sībawayh also heard an Arab say innī anā ibnuhā.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r8.anchor: قال الفرزدق # % منعت تميما منك أني أنا ابنها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r9.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r9.claim: For labbayka inna l-ḥamda, a genitive analysis after a deleted preposition is also strong, but Sībawayh identifies Khalīl's lām analysis as preferred, supported by wa-an al-masājida li-llāh.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابأن)#500/r9.anchor: والأول قول الخليل ويقوي ذلك قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p306/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when this verse was revealed, the only mosques on earth were the Sacred Mosque and the mosque of Aelia, Jerusalem.
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأن المساجد لله} قال: لم يكن يوم نزلت هذه الآية في الأرض مسجد إلا المسجد الحرام ومسجد إيليا بيت المقدس

DURR-FULL:v8p306/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r9.speaker: الأعمش
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports that the jinn asked permission to attend prayers in the Prophet’s mosque; the verse told them to pray without mixing with people.
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r9.anchor: عن الأعمش قال: قالت الجن: يا رسول الله ائذن لنا فنشهد معك الصلوات في مسجدك فأنزل الله {وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا}

DURR-FULL:v8p306/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r10.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the distant jinn asked how they could reach the mosque or witness prayer, and this verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: قالت الجن للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: كيف لنا أن نأتي المسجد ونحن ناؤون عنك أو كيف نشهد الصلاة ونحن ناؤون عنك فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v8p306/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Jews and Christians associated partners with God in synagogues and churches, so they were commanded to affirm His oneness.
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r11.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {وأن المساجد لله} الآية قال: إن اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا بيعهم وكنائسهم أشركوا بربهم فأمرهم أن يوحدوه

DURR-FULL:v8p306/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r12.claim: Qatada says Jews and Christians associated partners with God in their houses of worship, so the Prophet was commanded to devote invocation to God alone when entering the mosque.
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r12.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا} قال: كانت اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا بيعهم وكنائسهم أشركوا بالله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when this verse was revealed, the only mosques on earth were the Sacred Mosque and the mosque of Jerusalem.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وان المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله احدا قال : لم يكن يوم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r2.speaker: الأعمش
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash says the jinn asked the Prophet to join the prayers in his mosque, and this verse was revealed, instructing them to pray without mixing with people.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#3/r2.anchor: عن الاعمش قال : قالت الجن : يا رسول الله ائذن لنا فنشهد معك الصلوات في مسجدك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r12.speaker: القراء العشرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r12.claim: All ten readers open the hamza in “and the mosques belong to God.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r12.anchor: اتفق القراء العشرة على فتح الهمزة في { وأن المساجد لله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r13.claim: The clause coordinates with the nominative clause about the jinn listening in 72:1, so its content too was revealed to the Prophet and commanded for him to say.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p239/r13.anchor: ومضمونها مما أوحي به إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمر بأن يقوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari reports that Asim kasra-reads every initial إن/أن in the surah except the clause at 72:18.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r6.anchor: حكى الطبري عن عاصم أنه كان يكسر كل ألف في السورة من «أن» و «إن» إلا قوله تعالى: وأن المساجد لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi reports that Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open four hamzas in the surah and kasra-read the others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.anchor: وذكر أبو علي الفارسي أن ابن كثير وأبا عمرو فتحا أربعة أحرف من السورة وكسرا غير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.speaker: نافع، عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.claim: Nafi and Asim in the Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal transmissions agree on three openings but kasra-read the clause at 72:19 and the rest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.anchor: وأن نافعا وعاصما في رواية أبي بكر والمفضل وافقا في الثلاثة وكسرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.speaker: ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي، حفص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.claim: These readers open the surah's hamzas except after a saying or a consequential fa; this yields consensus on openings at 72:1, 72:16, and 72:18.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.anchor: وذكر أن ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي كانوا يقرأون كل ما في السورة بالفتح إلا ما جاء بعد قول أو فاء جزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
