IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.claim: Abu Hatim explains opening as coordination under passive أوحي, with clauses in the nominative; kasra is quotation, resumption, or follows a saying.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r12.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: أما الفتح فعلى أوحي، فهو كله في موضع رفع على ما لم يسم فاعله. وأما الكسر فحكاية وابتداء وبعد القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r1.claim: Hasan takes mosques to mean every place of prostration, designated or not, since the whole earth is a mosque for this community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r1.anchor: وقال الحسن: أراد كل موضع سجد فيه كان مخصوصا لذلك أو لم يكن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r2.claim: A report says the verse followed Quraysh's takeover of the Kaaba, assuring Muhammad that every place belongs to God and he may worship there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r2.anchor: وروي أن هذه الآية نزلت بسبب تغلب قريش على الكعبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r3.claim: Ibn Ata interprets mosques as the limbs used in prostration and gives the singular as masjid with a fatḥa on its jim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: «المساجد» : الآراب التي يسجد عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the jinn asked how they could pray with the Prophet from far away; the verse assured them worship is accepted wherever they are.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: نزلت الآية لأن الجن قالت يا رسول الله: كيف نشهد الصلاة معك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r5.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r5.claim: Al-Khalil reads the waw causally: because mosques belong to God, invoke no one with Him; he parallels 106:1, 3 and 21:92/23:52.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r5.anchor: وقال الخليل بن أحمد: معنى الآية، ولأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا أي لهذا السبب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r6.claim: Mosques are reserved for prayer, supplication, learning, and other acts solely for God; worldly conversation, using them as passages, and assigning others a share there are improper.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r6.anchor: و «المساجد» المخصوصة بينة التمكن في كونها لله تعالى فيصح أن تفرد للصلاة والدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r7.claim: After judging in Almeria's congregational mosque, he stopped hearing cases there because litigants' abuse, oaths, and quarrels violated the sanctuary's dignity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r7.anchor: ولقد قعدت للقضاء بين المسلمين في المسجد الجامع بالمرية مدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r1.claim: Al-masājid are the mosques, the houses of prayer; Qatāda says Jews and Christians associated partners when entering their worship places, so Muslims were commanded to worship God alone in mosques.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r1.anchor: أحدها أنها المساجد التي هي بيوت الصلوات قاله ابن عباس قال قتادة كانت اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا كنائسهم وبيعهم أشركوا فأمر الله عز وجل المسلمين أن يخلصوا له إذا دخلوا مساجدهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، ابن الأنباري، الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r2.claim: Al-masājid may mean the body parts on which a person prostrates, so they should not be used to prostrate to anyone but God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r2.anchor: والثاني الأعضاء التي يسجد عليها العبد قاله سعيد بن جبير وابن الأنباري وذكره الفراء فيكون المعنى لا تسجدوا عليها لغيره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r3.claim: Al-masājid may mean all regions of the earth; since all earth is a place for prostration, prostrate there only to its Creator.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r3.anchor: والثالث أن المراد بالمساجد ها هنا البقاع كلها قاله الحسن فيكون المعنى أن الأرض كلها مواضع للسجود فلا تسجدوا عليها لغير خالقها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r4.claim: Al-masājid may mean prostration itself: masjid is a verbal noun from sajada, and its singular has fatḥa on jīm; the command is to worship God alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p382#2/r4.anchor: والرابع أن المساجد السجود فإنه جمع مسجد يقال سجدت سجودا ومسجدا كما يقال ضربت في الأرض ضربا ومضربا ثم يجمع فيقال المساجد والمضارب قال ابن قتيبة فعلى هذا يكون واحدها مسجدا بفتح الجيم والمعنى أخلصوا له ولا تسجدا لغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r1.claim: God commands His servants to affirm His oneness in worship, invoke no one beside Him, and associate no one with Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى آمرا عباده أن يوحدوه في مجال عبادته، ولا يدعى معه أحد ولا يشرك به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r2.claim: Qatada says Jews and Christians associated partners with God when entering their churches and synagogues, so God commanded His Prophet to worship Him alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r2.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله: {وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا} قال: كانت اليهود والنصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when this verse was revealed, the only mosques on earth were the Sacred Mosque and the mosque of Ilya, Jerusalem.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا} قال: لم يكن يوم نزلت هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r4.speaker: الأعمش
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports that the jinn asked permission to attend prayers in the Prophet’s mosque; the verse tells them to pray without mixing with people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r4.anchor: وقال الأعمش: قالت الجن: يا رسول الله، ائذن لنا نشهد معك الصلوات في مسجدك. فأنزل الله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that distant jinn asked how they could reach the mosque and attend prayer while far from the Prophet; the verse was revealed in reply.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير،: {وأن المساجد لله} قال: قالت الجن لنبي (2) الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r6.claim: Ikrima says the verse was revealed concerning all mosques.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r6.anchor: وقال سفيان، عن خصيف، عن عكرمة: نزلت في المساجد كلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr interprets “mosques” as the bodily members used in prostration: they belong to God and must not prostrate to anyone else.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير. نزلت في أعضاء السجود، أي: هي لله فلا تسجدوا بها لغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r8.claim: The Prophet says he was commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead, hands, knees, and the ends of the feet; he gestured to his nose with his hands.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة أعظم

JISHUMI:v10p7121/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7121/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v10p7121/r1.claim: Jinn asked how they could attend the mosque and pray with the Prophet from far away; the verse was revealed in response.
JISHUMI:v10p7121/r1.anchor: قالت الجن للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: كيف لنا أن نأتي المسجد ونشهد معك الصلاة،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r1.claim: وأن المساجد may be part of the revelation, or the reason for the command not to invoke anyone alongside God in mosques.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r1.anchor: { وأن المساجد } من جملة الموحى . وقيل معناه : ولأن المساجد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r2.claim: No one may be invoked alongside God in mosques because they belong to Him exclusively and are devoted to His worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r2.anchor: أي : فلا تدعوا { مع الله أحدا } في المساجد ، لأنها لله خاصة ولعبادته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r3.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the mosques mean the whole earth, made a place of prostration for the Prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن : يعني الأرض كلها ؛ لأنها جعلت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مسجدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r4.claim: Another view identifies the mosques as the Sacred Mosque, the qibla toward which other mosques face.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r4.anchor: وقيل : المراد بها المسجد الحرام ، لأنه قبلة المساجد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r5.claim: The author links this to 2:114, which condemns preventing God's name from being mentioned in His mosques.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r5.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r6.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r6.claim: Qatada says Jews and Christians associated partners with God in their synagogues and churches, so Muslims were commanded to direct invocation to God alone in mosques.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r6.anchor: وعن قتادة : كان اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا بيعهم وكنائسهم أشركوا بالله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r7.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes the mosques to mean the seven bodily parts used in prostration.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r8.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r8.claim: The Prophet says he was commanded to prostrate on seven limbs: forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1235 ) ( أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة آراب : وهي الجبهة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r9.claim: Another view treats masājid as the plural of masjid, meaning prostration itself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p631/r9.anchor: وقيل : هي جمع مسجد وهو السجود

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r1.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r1.claim: Ibn Shajara says the mosques are the prayers offered to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r1.anchor: أحدها : يعني الصلوات لله , قاله ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r2.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r2.claim: Al-Rabi says the mosques are the body parts on which one prostrates to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنها الأعضاء التي يسجد عليها لله , قاله الربيع .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the mosques as God's houses for prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنها المساجد التي هي بيوت الله للصلوات , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r4.claim: Any place where a person prays is called a mosque because prostration occurs there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r4.anchor: الرابع : أنه كل موضع صلى فيه الإنسان , فإنه لأجل السجود فيه يسمى مسجدا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r5.claim: The prohibition means do not worship anyone alongside God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r5.anchor: أي فلا تعبدوا معه غيره , وفي سببه ثلاثة أقاويل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r6.speaker: الأعمش
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r6.claim: Al-A'mash relates that jinn asked permission to join the Prophet's prayer in his mosque, prompting the verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r6.anchor: أحدها : ما حكاه الأعمش أن الجن قالت : يا رسول الله ائذن لنا نشهد معك الصلاة في مسجدك , فنزلت هذه الآية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r7.claim: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali says the Meccan Hums pagans recited a talbiya assigning God a partner, so the verse forbade associating partners with Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r7.anchor: الثاني : ما حكاه أبو جعفر محمد بن علي أن الحمس من مشركي أهل مكة وهم كنانة وعامر وقريش كانوا يلبون حول البيت

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet entered the mosque right-foot first and prayed for release from the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r8.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا دخل المسجد قدم رجله اليمنى وقال

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r9.claim: The same report says he left the mosque left-foot first and asked for abundant good and an easy livelihood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r9.anchor: ( وإذا خرج من المسجد قدم رجله اليسرى وقال : ) اللهم صب الخير صبا ولا تنزع عني صالح ما أعطيتني

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r1.claim: The phrase belongs to the revelation, and the lām connects to “فلا تدعوا”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r1.anchor: من جملة الموحى أن اللام متعلقة بلا تدعوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r2.claim: Do not invoke anyone alongside God in mosques, which are devoted to God and His worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r2.anchor: في المساجد لأنها خالصة لله ولعبادته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r3.claim: An alternative takes “mosques” to mean the body parts used in prostration: forehead, hands, knees, and feet.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#3/r3.anchor: وقيل المساجد أعضاء السجود وهي الجبهة واليدان والركبتان والقدمان

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r23.claim: All reciters agree on fatḥa in wa-anna al-masājida lillāh; the source also lists wa-an qad ablaghū among the unanimous fatḥa readings.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r24.claim: All reciters agree that the hamza is kasra after speech, as in fa-qālū innā samiʿnā, qāla innamā adʿū rabbī, and qul innī lā adrī.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-3#5/r24.anchor: وكذلك لا خلاق في كسرها ما بعد القول

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r1.claim: The hamza is fatḥa; one parsing connects the clause to قل أوحي إلي, while al-Khalil reads it as because the mosques belong to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r1.anchor: بالفتح، قيل: هو مردود إلى قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r2.claim: On the first explanation, mosques are the houses that religious communities build for worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r2.anchor: والمراد البيوت التي تبنيها أهل الملل للعبادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the jinn asked how they could come to mosques and join the prayer while far away; the verse says they were built for remembrance and obedience to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: قالت الجن كيف لنا أن نأتي المساجد ونشهد معك الصلاة ونحن ناءون عنك؟

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r4.claim: Al-Hasan takes mosques to mean every place on earth, since the whole earth was made a place of prostration for the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: أراد بها كل البقاع لأن الأرض كلها مسجد للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r5.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r5.claim: Prophetic reports say to pray wherever one is and that wherever one prays is a mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r5.anchor:
للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، يقول:
" أينما كنتم فصلوا "
" فأينما صليتم فهو مسجد "

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r6.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r6.claim: A sahih report says the earth was made a mosque and a means of purification for the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r6.anchor:
وفي الصحيح:
" وجعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وطهورا "

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وطلق بن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and Talq ibn Habib identify the mosques as the limbs used in prostration, which must not be used to prostrate to other than God, their giver.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r7.anchor: أراد بالمساجد الأعضاء التي يسجد عليها العبد

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r8.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r8.claim: Ata says the limbs commanded to prostrate should not be humbled before anyone but their Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r8.anchor: مساجدك: أعضاؤك التي أمرت أن تسجد عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet was commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead, nose, hands, knees, and toes.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r9.anchor:
وفي الصحيح عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة أعظم: الجبهة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r10.speaker: العباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r10.claim: Al-Abbas reports the Prophet said that when a servant prostrates, seven joints prostrate with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r10.anchor:
وقال العباس قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إذا سجد العبد سجد معه سبعة آراب "

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r11.claim: Al-Hasan also says mosques means the prayers, since prostration belongs to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r11.anchor: وقيل: المساجد هي الصلوات أي لأن السجود لله. قاله الحسن أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r12.claim: If mosques means places, the singular is masjid with kasra on the jim, though al-Farraʾ also reports a form with fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r12.anchor: فإن جعلت المساجد المواضع فواحدها مسجد بكسر الجيم، ويقال بالفتح حكاه الفراء.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r13.claim: If mosques means bodily limbs, the singular masjad has fatḥa on the jim.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r13.anchor: وإن جعلتها الأعضاء لواحدها مسجد بفتح الجيم.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r14.claim: Another analysis treats masājid as the plural of masjid meaning prostration, a verbal noun like madrab for traveling in search of livelihood.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع مسجد وهو السجود

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas says the mosques are Mecca, the direction of prayer, called mosques because everyone prostrates toward it.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المساجد هنا مكة التي هي القبلة وسميت مكة المساجد لأن كل أحد يسجد إليها.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r16.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the first explanation, that mosques are houses of worship, and says it is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r16.anchor: والقول الأول أظهر هذه الأقوال إن شاء الله، وهو مروي عن ابن عباس رحمه الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r17.claim: The possessive attribution to God expresses honor and distinction; the sacred House is then singled out.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18/r17.anchor: قوله تعالى: { لله } إضافة تشريف وتكريم، ثم خص بالذكر منها البيت العتيق فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r1.claim: God’s command to purify His House is related to the mosque discussion.

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r2.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r2.claim: The Prophet said journeys should be undertaken only to three mosques; hadith authorities transmitted it, and Qurtubi says it was discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r2.anchor: لا تعمل المطي إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r3.claim: Prayer in the Prophet’s mosque is better than a thousand elsewhere, except in the Sacred Mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r3.anchor: صلاة في مسجدي هذا خير من ألف صلاة فيما سواه إلا المسجد الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r4.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports through a sound route that prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than a hundred prayers in the Prophet’s mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد روى من طريق لا بأس بها

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r5.claim: Qurtubi affirms that further prayer-reward report as authentic through reliable transmitters, as explained in Ibrahim.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r5.anchor: قلت: هو صحيح بنقل العدل عن العدل حسب ما بيناه

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r6.claim: Mosques belong to and are honored by God, yet may be named after people for identification; attribution can reflect location or endowment.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r6.anchor: المساجد وإن كانت لله ملكا وتشريفا فإنها قد تنسب إلى غيره تعريفا

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r7.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r7.claim: A sound hadith describes the Prophet racing trained and untrained horses between named sites, illustrating local mosque naming.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r7.anchor: وفي صحيح الحديث: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سابق بين الخيل التي أضمرت

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r8.claim: The community agrees mosques, bridges, and cemeteries may be endowed, but jurists dispute endowing other property.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r8.anchor: ولا خلاف بين الأمة في تحبيس المساجد والقناطر والمقابر وإن اختلفوا في تحبيس غير ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r9.claim: Permitted mosque uses include dividing funds, sharing charity among the poor, detention, restraining captives, sleeping, housing the sick, neighbor access, and nonfalse poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r9.anchor: فإنه تجوز القسمة فيها للأموال. ويجوز وضع الصدقات فيها على رسم الاشتراك

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r10.claim: The prohibition rebukes polytheists for invoking others alongside God in the Sacred Mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r10.anchor: هذا توبيخ للمشركين في دعائهم مع الله غيره في المسجد الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r11.claim: Mujahid says Jews and Christians practiced associationism in churches and synagogues, so believers must devote worship to God in every mosque and worship no idol there.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كانت اليهود والنصارى إذا دخلوا كنائسهم وبيعهم أشركوا بالله

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r12.claim: Another view reserves mosques for remembrance of God, not mockery, commerce, assemblies, passageways, or giving others a share in worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أفردوا المساجد لذكر الله، ولا تتخذوها هزوا ومتجرا ومجلسا

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r1.claim: The Prophet said to answer anyone announcing a lost item in a mosque with a prayer that it not be returned, since mosques were not built for that.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r1.anchor: من نشد ضالة في المسجد فقولوا لا ردها الله عليك فإن المساجد لم تبن لهذا

QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r2.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r2.claim: A report through al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet entered right-foot first and prayed for release from the Fire, then exited left-foot first asking for abundant good and lasting blessing; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:18#3/r2.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
